subject: Post-call: context profiling & unit-econ targets for pricing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@neurolytics.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@glimmerco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: context profiling & unit-econ targets for pricing

Thanks for the call earlier — good discussion. Quick recap and a couple of concrete asks so we can model pricing scenarios and get you an apples-to-apples $/1M token target.

Summary of what we heard today
- Primary flow: user prompt -> short assistant response (FAQ-style) ~ short completions; second flow: long-form summarization of uploaded docs (long outputs).
- Expected peak concurrency: low (10-20 qps), but bursty.
- Data residency: US-only.

Information we need to finalize pricing/forecast (small asks, please reply inline):
1) Average prompt tokens per request (mean, 95th pct) — helps with prefix caching and batching assumptions.
2) Average completion tokens per request (mean, 95th pct).
3) Distribution of long-context requests: percent of requests that need 8k vs 32k vs 128k context windows. If you don’t know exact, a rough % is fine (e.g., 85% 8k, 14% 32k, 1% 128k).
4) Monthly projected token volume (prompt vs completion). If you only have daily active users and avg requests per user we can convert.
5) Target unit-econ: what is your target $/1M tokens (or a budget range)?

What we'll provide next
- A cost sensitivity table: per million token cost across three provisioning profiles (hosted burst, dedicated reserved, private) and three context bands (8k/32k/128k).
- A recommended serving config (batching, cache TTLs, quantization profile) and an expected per-request latency band.

Attachments: sending a simple context_profile template we discussed so you can drop numbers in.
[Attachment: context_profile.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 28KB)]

Next steps
- Please fill the sheet and return (or reply with numbers).
- If you prefer, we can run a short PoC for a week to collect real token mix and then finalize pricing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up call Thursday if that helps.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@neurolytics.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 18:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: context profiling & unit-econ targets for pricing

Thanks Marissa — nice summary. Answers inline below.

1) Avg prompt tokens: mean ~1,150; 95th pct ~2,800. Prompts are often structured (system + user) so the prefix can be ~300 tokens of system/context, rest is user.
2) Avg completion tokens: mean ~380; 95th pct ~2,500. The majority are short (100–400 tokens), but about 4% are long summaries (1k–5k).
3) Long-context distribution (rough estimates):
   - 8k: 91%
   - 32k: 8.6%
   - 128k: 0.4% (very rare, only for enterprise analytic export jobs)
4) Monthly projected volume (current year target):
   - Prompts: 340M tokens/month
   - Completions: 115M tokens/month
   (We expect 3x growth YoY; these are conservative launch numbers.)
5) Target unit-econ: we’re targeting $65–$90 per 1M tokens (combined prompt+completion), ideally closer to $70. If dedicated reserved pricing brings that down for our volume, we can discuss a 12-month commit.

Additional notes:
- Latency SLO target: p95 endpoint latency < 350ms for short flows. For long-context summarization we can accept higher latency (up to 2.5s p95).
- Security: SOC2 + encryption at rest is required.

Happy to fill the sheet with exact daily breakdown once I loop in ops (Sara copied).

— Liam
Liam O'Connor | VP Product, NeuroLytics
liam@neurolytics.ai | +1 (617) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 19:10:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Post-call: context profiling & unit-econ targets for pricing

Looping you both in with Liam's numbers. Key takeaways for pricing model:
- Volume: ~455M tokens/month combined (prompts + completions) — we should model 3 forecast bands: conservative (current), ramp (6–12 months), and committed (12+ months).
- Token mix heavily skewed to 8k but non-trivial 32k usage and tiny 128k tail. That will affect memory/instance sizing and cost per token.
- Target $/1M: $65–$90, ideal $70. We need to see if we can meet that with a dedicated reserved proposal or if hosted with aggressive batching + caching can get us there.

Request for Ben/Connor:
- Ben: run quick back-of-envelope unit-econ for hosted vs dedicated assuming 91% 8k / 8.6% 32k / 0.4% 128k and the volumes Liam gave. Include separate lines for prompt vs completion pricing.
- Connor: can you draft a concise config for the PoC that shows: model (open checkpoint), batch window, cache TTL, target p95 latency, and telemetry we'll collect? Put this in pricing_scenarios.pdf and attach.

I'll pull together the HubSpot deal and a pricing intro doc to share with Liam + Sara. If we can show a committed 12-month uplift that hits $70/1M, they indicated they'd be open to reserved capacity.

[Attachment: pricing_scenarios.pdf (application/pdf, 92KB)]

— Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: context profiling & unit-econ targets for pricing

Got it — will run three scenarios this morning and share numbers by EOD (hosted burst, dedicated 6-month commit, dedicated 12-month commit).
Quick callouts so our outputs line up with sales ask:
- Include a column for effective $/1M tokens after accounting for cache hit rate. If they adopt a 20% prefix cache hit we can show meaningful savings.
- Model the 128k tail as an opt-in "batch export" SKU (higher $/1M but low frequency); that usually satisfies finance.
- I'll include a sensitivity where completion-heavy mix (e.g., 20% longer completions) increases unit cost by ~15–25%.

Will add HubSpot link and the draft DocuSign for a term sheet stub once numbers look good.

— Ben
